welcome: 👋 Hi! I'm a notification bot for GitHub and GitLab. Quick start: 1. Enable Topics in the group and make me an admin 2. /configure — set up topics and the message look 3. /connect <repo_url> — get the webhook URL and secret /help — list of commands
help: 📚 Available commands: /start — getting started /configure — set up forum topics and the message look /connect <url> — connect a GitHub/GitLab repository /disconnect <url> — disconnect a repository /status — chat settings, topics and repositories /lang en|ru — change the notification language /version — bot version /help — this help
unknown_command: Sorry, I only understand commands. Type /help
send_failed: ❌ Failed to send message to chat %d: %v
panel_started: 🖥 Web panel listening on http://%s (open it through an SSH tunnel)
webhook_duplicate: ♻️ Duplicate webhook already delivered, skipping | platform=%s | event=%s | delivery=%s
delivery_log_failed: ⚠️ Failed to update the delivery log: %v
invalid_retention: ❌ Invalid DELIVERIES_RETENTION_DAYS %q: use a whole number of days, 0 keeps the log forever
configure_chat_not_admin: ❌ I need to be an administrator to create topics. Grant me admin rights first.
configure_chat_success:
✅ Forum topics created successfully!

You can now configure which events go to which topic.
configure_chat_how_to_use: 💡 Next step: connect a repository with /connect <url>. Each event type will be posted to its own topic; unmapped events go to General.
failed_save_topic_to_storage: ❌ Failed to save topic '%s' to storage: %v
failed_to_map_event_to_storage: ❌ Failed to map event '%s' to topic %d: %v
failed_to_check_bot_admin_status: ❌ Failed to check bot admin status: %v
connect_invalid_url: ❌ Invalid URL. Send a repository URL like https://github.com/user/repo or https://gitlab.com/group/project (self-hosted GitLab works too).
connect_github: 💡 GitHub setup: 1. Repository → Settings → Webhooks → Add webhook 2. Payload URL: the URL above 3. Content type: application/json 4. Secret: the secret above 5. Events: Send me everything (or pick the ones you need)
connect_gitlab: 💡 GitLab setup: 1. Project → Settings → Webhooks → Add new webhook 2. URL: the URL above 3. Secret token: the secret above 4. Triggers: Push, Tag push, Merge request, Issues, Comments, Pipeline, Releases
connect_test: 🧪 Test it: after saving, GitHub sends a ping event — a confirmation will appear here. Or run: curl -X POST %s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-GitHub-Event: ping" -d '{}'
